questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
It was important to find a place with great academic opportunities in my academic field and and with a vibrant and multidisciplinary environment. 
It was also important for me to live in a larger English speaking city where I could learn from the culture and gain new connections, both on a personal but also professional level.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
It was pretty difficult at the beginning. I arrived 3 weeks before the program started and it was difficult to gain information before the program started. I visited the UCEAP office at UCLA 3 times at my first visit at UCLA, but they didn't know they were representing the UCEAP program and kept sending me different places, until I called the UCEAP program and was insured it was that office. 
I had great difficulties finding a place to live and didn't get much help to find a solution.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Exchange student orientation

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer:
There was a lot of confusion about which orientations I should attend, the one I had signed up for, wasn't registered at the right place, so I had to attend to different ones plus the one for exchange students, even though I still don't know if I had to attend all three. 
We didn't get basic knowledge such as what platform is used by the professors for homework, etc.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: No, I lived 5 different places in L.A. before I moved to UCHA next to UCLA.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
It can be very difficult to find a place to live in L.A. if you are foreign and staying less than a year. 
There are a lot of scammers, most landlords won´t accept you if you are foreign because we don't use credit scores and recommendation from former landlords, and they don't accept foreign co-signer. 
UCHA is a great alternative since it's cheap and near campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was fine. I had some problems getting access to the grad courses since I had to get acceptance from the professors first and they weren't all that willing to cooperate. But then other professors where were helpful.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You go to bruin learn -> course registrations and then you can plan your schedule and sign up for the courses you want to attend.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: not really

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: pretty succesful. In the first quarter I had a harder time getting the courses I wanted and that was accepted by my program at home, but at my second quarter I had better luck.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be persistent and email the professors teaching the courses you want, sometimes more than once. Attend faculty events and talk with the professors there, that help me getting some of the courses I wanted

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The BA level courses had more weekly coursework and TA discussion groups every week. I felt like they were a little lower level than my BA classes back home. The exams are way shorter than at UCPH. Each class has a clear description of what's expected of the student and how the class is graded. The KA classes level was very theoretical and high level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I like that there was a structured plan for each course and that you know what's expected of you and what the grade you on.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Ethnomusicology: African american music ensemble 161P is a gospel choir for all levels. It's a great way to meet other people and gain insights in the gospel music culture.

questions.answer: Public transportation is very inexpensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything you can imagine. there so many clubs and events!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend any club or sports activity you find interesting. Stay posted on the MYUCLA website and calendar and sign up for all the newsletters. The international office host a lot of great events for international student where you can meet other exchange students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go out and explore L.A. Westwood is not the greatest representation of Los Angeles. Visit some of the national forests and drive up the coast.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I think It was easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to strangers and the people in you class.   Go to event and talk to the people that are there. L.A. is a great city full of free events you can go to each week, I met a lot of amazing people by just talking to strangers and trying new stuff.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: It's a more outgoing culture.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That itt's a more outgoing culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be open minded. 
Ucla is big and there is a lot of systems/ bureaucracy, but once you figure it out it's not that difficult. 
Take advantages of all the opportunities and great organisations and clubs.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
It will be more expensive then you think. 
You can find most information on bruinlearn - Learn how to navigate it!
Wise is a great bank alternative. 
UCHA COOP is a great housing opportunity. 
Mint mobile is the cheapest option. 
If you need to use cashapps you have to open an American bank account.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met and the new perspectives and knowledge I gained.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding a place to live of campus.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
